```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)


library("dplyr") # data cleaning and handling
library("modelsummary") # outputting results where needed
library(tidyr) 
library(broom)
library(purrr)
library(srvyr) # used for logit regressions with complex survey designs
library(svyVGAM) # used for PPO regressions with complex survey designs 
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)

# Load project configuration
source(here::here("R", "load_config.R"))
cfg <- load_config()

# Construct input file path
input_2024 <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_2024_1year
)

input_2019 <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_2019_1year
)

  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$outout_file_ACS_1year_means
)

  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_ACS_1year_IncDis
)


## independent variables to be used in the regressions below.  This means you only
## need to update them here.

x_vector <- ("HHSize + ChildPresent + SeniorPresent + AGE + LF + SEX + ChildPresent*HHSize+AGE*LF") 

#stopifnot(file.exists(input_2019))
stopifnot(file.exists(input_2024))
stopifnot(file.exists(input_means))
stopifnot(file.exists(input_dis))

```

## load the 2024 data and create the formula 
 
```{r}

ACS_1year_2024 <- read.csv(file.path(input_2024)) ## loads 2024 data

#restoring ordered factor nature to the ordered factor varriable
ACS_1year_2024$IncCat <- ordered(ACS_1year_2024$IncCat, levels = paste0("Inc", 1:14))

ACS_1year_means <-read.csv(file.path(input_means))

ACS_1year_dis <-read.csv(file.path(input_dis))

Weighted_IPUMS <-as_survey(ACS_1year_2024, id=CLUSTER,
                           weights=HHWT,
                           strata=STRATA,
                           nest=TRUE)

## Goal here is to test the Partial Proportional Odds Model (PPO).  This model allows you 
## to take advantage of the fact that you have ordinal data for variables which
## meet the parallel lines assumption, and let them vary randomly for the variables
## which do not meet that assumption. In order to test if we should use a PPO
## we would normally use a Brant Test.  That test effectively looks at if the coefficients 
## (B) are close enough in the separate logistic models to have parallel slopes
## after accounting for difference from sampling. However we have a complex survey
## design featuring stratification which does not line up with the random sampling
## assumption in the Brant test. This modification of the Brant test which uses
## R's survey package to introduce the sampling weights.  The blog post detailing it
## can be found here https://notstatschat.rbind.io/2023/02/09/checking-proportionality-of-odds/

# set our formula, this saves us from retyping it for all the individual logistic
# regressions and lets us test alternative specifications


formula <- as.formula(
  paste("IncCat ~", x_vector)
)

 
 

``` 
## Test which variables do or do not meet parallel lines assumption 
```{r}
#setting up the ordered logit model with weights
m1 <-svyolr(formula, design = Weighted_IPUMS)

K<-length(m1$lev) # acquire levels of the ordered category IncCat
P<-length(m1$coef) # acquire # of coefficients which is 6 but we can change the model

#get influence function which allows covariance matrix to be computed
#this fist block defines the influence function
get_infl <-function(k,formula,design){
  y<-formula[[2]]
  formula[[2]]<-bquote(I(as.numeric(.(y))>.(k)))
  mk<-svyglm(formula, design, family= quasibinomial, influence=TRUE) #quasibinomial is the svglm package's logistic regression
  list(coef(mk), attr(mk, "influence"))
  }

#this second block calls it and get the covariance matrix
# lapply applied the function over each of our levels, running a binomial
# regression for each level of the function, except the last which is the omitted category
# combined_v is the variance covariance matrix based on the complex survey design totals
fits<-lapply(1:(K-1), function(k) get_infl(k, formula, Weighted_IPUMS))
infs<-do.call(cbind,lapply(fits,"[[",2))
combined_V<- vcov(svytotal(infs/weights(Weighted_IPUMS), Weighted_IPUMS))

# now we extract the coefficients we care about to make the comparison
conditional_V<- lapply(1:P, 
                       function(p) 1/diag(solve(combined_V[c(p+1+(0:(K-2))*(P+1)), c(p+1+(0:(K-2))*(P+1))])))
coefs<-lapply(fits,"[[",1)


## An initial visual test, if the point estimates on the coefficients are all within
## one anther's error bars we are probably ok to use the ordinal model for that
## coefficient, otherwise that var fails the parallel lines assumption
## we can then make a modified formula and run it through the Brant test located
## in the next code block

res <- data.frame(
  variable = rep(names(coefs[[1]])[-1], each = K - 1),
  cutpoint = rep(names(m1$zeta), P),
  estimate = as.vector(do.call(rbind, coefs)[,-1]),
  se = sqrt(do.call(c, conditional_V))
)

res$cutpoint <- factor(
  res$cutpoint,
  levels = rev(names(m1$zeta)),
  ordered = TRUE
)

res$lower <- res$estimate - 1.96 * res$se
res$upper <- res$estimate + 1.96 * res$se

p<-ggplot(res,aes(y=cutpoint,col=cutpoint))+
  geom_point(aes(x=estimate))+
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin=lower,xmax=upper))+
  facet_wrap(~variable,scales="free")+
  theme(legend.position="none")+
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=z),linetype="dotted",
             data.frame(z=m1$coef,variable=names(coefs[[1]])[-1]))
print(p)

```


## modified Brant test
```{r}
## here is then the modified Brant test which looks at how far away the 
## unconstrained betas are from one another specifically testing if
## B_{kp}=T_k*B_p 
## T_k is a term for individual levels around the cut points.  
## basically we want to know if the betas from running the Ordered Logit model
## look like the Betas we get when we run the individual logit models, just
## doing in that in a more statistically rigorous way which accounts for 
## variance in the samples and complex survey sampling.


# Rerun the model in case the previous block was not run
m1 <-svyolr(formula, design = Weighted_IPUMS)

#terms needed for the Brant Test
K <- length(m1$lev)  # Acquire levels of the ordered category IncCat
P <- length(m1$coef) # Acquire number of coefficients 

# Get influence function which allows covariance matrix to be computed
# This fist block defines the influence function
get_infl <- function(k, formula, design) {
  y <- formula[[2]]
  formula[[2]] <- bquote(I(as.numeric(.(y)) > .(k)))
  mk <- svyglm(formula, design, family = quasibinomial, influence = TRUE)
  list(coef(mk), attr(mk, "influence"))
}

# This second block calls the influence function and get the covariance matrix
# lapply applied the function over each of our K-1 cut-points, running a binomial
# regression for each level of the function, except the last which is the omitted category
 
fits <- lapply(1:(K - 1), function(k) get_infl(k, formula, Weighted_IPUMS))
infs <- do.call(cbind, lapply(fits, "[[", 2))
combined_V <- vcov(svytotal(infs / weights(Weighted_IPUMS), Weighted_IPUMS))

coefs <- lapply(fits, "[[", 1)

# Extract slope coefficients (excluding intercepts) and their joint covariance matrix
B <- do.call(c, lapply(coefs, "[", -1))
intercept_idx <- 1 + (0:(K - 2)) * (P + 1)
VarB <- combined_V[-intercept_idx, -intercept_idx]

# Tests whether slopes scale proportionally across cut-points: B_{kp} = T_k * B_p
# creates a matrix so our output exists for all variables not just the join model

D_dir <- diag(P)
for (k in 2:(K - 1)) {
  D_dir <- rbind(D_dir, diag(P))
}
D_dir <- cbind(D_dir, matrix(0, nrow = P * (K - 1), ncol = K - 2))

for (k in 1:(K - 2)) {
  D_dir[(P * k) + (1:P), P + k] <- coefs[[k + 1]][-1]
}

VarBinv <- solve(VarB)
deltahat <- solve(t(D_dir) %*% VarBinv %*% D_dir, t(D_dir) %*% VarBinv %*% B)
VarDelta <- solve(t(D_dir) %*% VarBinv %*% D_dir)

i <- P + (1:(K - 2))
brantTest_dir <- as.numeric(deltahat[i] %*% solve(VarDelta[i, i]) %*% deltahat[i])
p_dir <- pchisq(brantTest_dir, df = (K - 2), lower.tail = FALSE)

# Standard Omnibus & Per-Coefficient Brant Tests (Brant 1990, Section 2)
# Tests strict equality of slopes across cut-points: B_{1p} = B_{2p} = ... = B_{(K-1)p}
# E.G. are all the individual coefficients from the logit model the same for each category? 

D_std <- matrix(0, nrow = P * (K - 2), ncol = P * (K - 1))

for (k in 1:(K - 2)) {
  row_idx <- ((k - 1) * P + 1):(k * P)
  col_idx_1 <- 1:P
  col_idx_k <- (k * P + 1):((k + 1) * P)
  
  D_std[row_idx, col_idx_1] <- diag(P)
  D_std[row_idx, col_idx_k] <- -diag(P)
}

# Standard Omnibus Test, tests all coefficents jointly
diff_B <- D_std %*% B
Var_diff <- D_std %*% VarB %*% t(D_std)
X2_omnibus <- as.numeric(t(diff_B) %*% solve(Var_diff) %*% diff_B)
df_omnibus <- P * (K - 2)
p_omnibus <- pchisq(X2_omnibus, df = df_omnibus, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Build results table starting with Directional Omnibus and Standard Omnibus
coef_names <- names(m1$coef)
results <- data.frame(
  Test = c("Omnibus (Directional)", "Omnibus (Standard)", coef_names),
  Chi2 = NA,
  df = NA,
  p_value = NA
)

results[1, 2:4] <- c(brantTest_dir, K - 2, p_dir)
results[2, 2:4] <- c(X2_omnibus, df_omnibus, p_omnibus)

# Loop through each individual coefficient test
for (p in 1:P) {
  p_rows <- seq(from = p, to = P * (K - 2), by = P)
  D_p <- D_std[p_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  
  diff_p <- D_p %*% B
  Var_p <- D_p %*% VarB %*% t(D_p)
  
  X2_p <- as.numeric(t(diff_p) %*% solve(Var_p) %*% diff_p)
  df_p <- K - 2
  p_val <- pchisq(X2_p, df = df_p, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  results[p + 2, 2:4] <- c(X2_p, df_p, p_val)
}

# Format and print output
# Null is that the parallel lines assumption holds 
# Note that Brant actually warns against using the Omnibus test, its included for
# completeness

results$Chi2 <- round(results$Chi2, 3)
results$p_value <- round(results$p_value, 4)
print(results, row.names = FALSE)

# clear these away to rerun the Brant test later.  We could rename them below if
# we want to have both Brant tests for some reason 
 rm(K, P, fits, infs, combined_V, conditional_V, coefs, D, B, VarB, VarBinv, deltahat, VarDelta, brantTest)


```



Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
```{r}
## based on the visual test and confirming with the Brant test, we modify the 
## model.  The formula remains the same but under family we add the option
## parallel = TRUE ~ and follow with the variables that should be treated
## as having a parallel trend with the syntax ~ X1+X2+...+Xn where X are our  
## parallel variables.  We can flip this to parallel = FALSE and then specify 
## the non-parallel variables instead if there are many of them

ppo_model <- svy_vglm(
  formula = formula,
  family = cumulative(link = "logitlink", parallel = TRUE ~ AGE + SEX),
  design = Weighted_IPUMS
)

## to do, create an un-stacked model summary table for easy viewing.  
## log-odds presented here not easy to interpret anyways so this is a low priority 

```
